absolute and relative claim maps are compared against each other rather than an independent oracle, so the case cannot fail on a narrowing regression; at base both return the whole set and only the missing path key reddens it.
an over-budget single path empties the page while next_cursor stays at the unchanged offset, so a paging caller loops on an empty page forever.

FINDING docs/evidence/fragments/the-mcp-answers-the-question-asked/the-scopes-read-narrows-to-its-path.html:105 non-blocking: the caveat states the served default read lands at 23,606 characters against the 24,000 row, while line 71 of the same fragment and served-scopes-default.log:6 record 23,026 for that call, and no log under the run directory carries 23,606; a reader reconciling the evidence record against the artefact it cites meets two figures for one measurement, and the commit that rewrote these figures to match the logs missed this one.
FINDING tests/test_the_scopes_read_narrows_to_its_path.py:280 non-blocking: assert absolute["claim_map"] == relative["claim_map"] compares two returns of the code under test against each other rather than against an independent source, so it holds whatever the narrowing does as long as both spellings are treated alike; at the base revision both calls return the whole claim set and the case reddens only on the missing path key asserted at :281, so this line is not a regression guard for the behaviour it is named after.
FINDING reckon/mcp_views.py:4260 non-blocking: when one path's owners alone exceed the 24,000 row the loop at :4265 empties the page and still returns next_cursor = _cursor(offset) with offset unchanged, so a paging caller receives an empty page with the same cursor indefinitely; the fix needs a floor of one path per page, or a terminal cursor when nothing fits, so an over-budget path fails loudly instead of looping.
